nodes.label: postgresDialect
nodes.rationale: Classifies SQL failures by SQLSTATE and never by message text - the property the two pg-wire certifications exist to prove.

nodes.label: YugabyteDB service
nodes.rationale: yugabyted start --daemon=false --background=false brings up a single-node cluster with YSQL enabled and stays in the foreground so compose can manage the lifecycle. First boot initializes the system catalogs and takes noticeably longer than any other image in the matrix, hence start_period 60s and 60 retries.

nodes.label: YugabyteDB runner service
nodes.rationale: PG_URL postgres://yugabyte@yugabytedb:5433/yugabyte with WIRE_LABEL yugabytedb; the yugabyte user and database exist out of the box without a password in the default unauthenticated configuration.

nodes.label: Probe the container's own address, not 127.0.0.1
nodes.rationale: YSQL listens on 5433, not 5432, and comes up well after the process starts. yugabyted binds every service to the node's advertise address, so loopback never listens and a 127.0.0.1 probe fails forever even once the cluster is fully up. That is what happened: the container went unhealthy after a clean YugabyteDB Started line, compose refused to start the runner on the unmet service_healthy condition, and this certification silently never ran at all while looking like a slow image.

nodes.label: Classify by SQLSTATE, never by message text
nodes.rationale: Yugabyte is the more interesting of the two certifications because it is known to reword some Postgres error messages (yugabyte/yugabyte-db#9294). That is harmless here precisely because postgresDialect classifies by SQLSTATE - this suite is what proves it. Matching the code was necessary but not sufficient: at SERIALIZABLE the losing append is aborted as 40001 before it ever reaches the primary key (#479).
